newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Chirac details plans for Euro-Latin summit.
newsitem.headline: Chirac details plans for Euro-Latin summit.

text.p: The European Union and Latin America will lay the groundwork at a proposed summit next year for a three-pronged political, economic and education partnership, French President Jacques Chirac said on Sunday.

Chirac, on the penultimate stage of a tour of five Latin American countries, detailed proposals he made earlier this week in Brasilia for the first ever summit of leaders of the EU and all of Latin America.
He said the two regions should develop a political, as well as economic partnership in order to reflect the world's political globalisation.

"Globalisation is also political... Political partnership is necessary. There are no longer any more or less important nations, that is the past," he said in a speech in the capital of Paraguay, an impoverished country of five million people.
Chirac said education was the third major issue to be discussed at the summit "in order to help young people get a spot in a society that is increasingly technical".

"Those who do not have the knowledge will be marginalised," he said. Chirac has launched a campaign at home to improve education in order to curb record unemployment affecting more acutely people under 25.

At a news conference later, Chirac dismissed doubts that his call for a summit was a personal initiative without EU approval. He said he had discussed it with German and Spanish leaders as well as with the Netherlands which holds the EU's rotating presidency, and had informed the European Commission.

He repeated that a partnership with Europe was not aimed at challenging U.S. influence in Latin America, saying it would add to rather than harm plans for integration of North and South America in a free trade area by 2005.

Chirac heaped praise on Mercosur, the customs union grouping Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay, saying it had emerged in six years since its foundation as the world's fourth economic power. "It will be the third largest power tomorrow," he said.

His trip has centred on reviving France's economic exchanges with Latin America, and he said he planned to visit all the region's countries before his term ends in 2002. He was due to leave later in the day for Argentina.

Keen to boost French investment in Paraguay, which is located at the geographic centre of Mercosur's major road and waterway infrastructure projects, he awarded the country a stamp of good behaviour despite reports that the end of Gen. Alfredo Stroessner's 36-year dictatorship eight years ago and the return to democracy had failed to eradicate widespread corruption.
He said such reports provided excuses for businessmen who argued that "the water is too cold to swim" because they had cold feet about investing.
"Let me tell you the mafia is all over the world...even among Vatican staff," he said.
"I wish all countries France trades with had as little mafia as Paraguay," he said. "Paraguay has an excellent image in Europe."
"There is mafia and smuggling all over the world.
The head of Paraguay's state auditing body, Daniel Fretes Ventre, said in an interview with Reuters last month he suspected President Juan Carlos Wasmosy of covering up corruption in government.
